FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 14 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Information Systems and Software Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. Assistance has been derived in formulating this standard from ISOIIEC DP 2382-14 `Information technology - Vocabulary - Part 14 : Reliability. maintenance and availability', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ).

INFORMATION PROCESSING SYSTEMS -VOCABULARY
PART 1 SCOPE 1.1 This Standard related to reliability, 2 RELIABILITY ( Part 14 ) covers the terms maintenance and availability. AND FAULTS 14 RELIABILITY, MAINTENANCE 2.9 Fault An abnormal condition that causes a reduction in or loss of capability of a functional unit to perform its required function. 2.10 Failure The termination of the ability of a functional to perform its required function. 2.11 Failure The frequency unit time. 2.12 Defect The lack of or the deficiency in a characteristic essential in satisfying appl,cab!e requirements, w!lich affects, or is likely to affect, the ability of a functional unit to perform its required function. A defect is typically considered as built in during the design or manufacturing of a functional unit. 2.13 Program-Sensitive Fault Rate of failures of a functional unit per unit AND AVAILABILITY

2.1 Product Assurance The verification of the conformity of a product with applicable objectives, standards, specifications and other requirements throughout the life of the product. 2.2 Reliability The ability of a functional unit to perform required function under stated conditions for stated period of time. 2.3 Duiability The ability of a functional unit to perform a required function under given conditions of use and maintenance, until the end of the useful life, or until it becomes unsuitable for economic or technological reasons. 2.4 Mean Time Between Failures ( MTBF ) For a stated period in the life of a functional unit, the average interval of time between consecutive failures under stated conditions. This term is used for a repairable system. 2.5 Mean Time to First Failure ( MTTF ) For a stated period in the life of a functional unit, the average time interval until a failure is expected to occur under stated conditions. This term is used for a non-repairable system. 2.6 Mean Time to Recovery ( MTTR ) For a stated period in the life of a functional unit, required for corrective the average time interval maintenance under stated conditions. 2.7 Mean Down Time ( MDT ) For a stated period in the life of a .functional the average value of the expected down under stated conditions. 2.8 Mistake Error unit, time a a

A fault that is revealed as a result of the execution of some particular sequence of instructions. 2.14 Data-Sensitive Fault proces-

A fault that is revealed as a result of the sing of a particular pattern of d&u. 3 MAINTENANCE 3.1 Maintenance

A set of activities intended to keep a functional unit in, or to restore it to, a state in which it can perform its required function. Maintenance includes activities such as tests, measurements, replacements, adjustments and repairs. 3.2 Maintenance Tree

A graph showing the hierarchy of maintenance activities that can be performed on a functional uni? and the conditions for choosing among them. 3.3 Maintainability/Serviceability The ease with which maintenance of a functional accordance with unit can be prrformed in prescribed requirements. 3.4 Maintenance Support

A human action that can produce an unintended result. The term `error' is defined in IS 1885 ( Part 52/Set 2 ) : 1980 Electrotechnical vocabulary : Part 52 Data processing, Set 2 Arithmetic and logic operations. 1

The provision by a maintenance organization of the services required to maintain a functional unit.

IS 13557 ( Part 14) : 199:3 3.5 Corrective Maintenance specifically to overcome 4.4 Operating Time That part of operable functional unit is operated. 4.5 Down Time The time during which a functional unit cannot be used because of a fault. Down time can result from a fault within the functional unit or from an environtnental fault; in the former case, the down time is also called the inoperable time. 4.6 Idle Time That part of operable time when a functional is not being used. in accordance 4.7 Program Production Time That part of operating time during computer program is executed. 4.8 System Test Time That part of operating time during which the functional unit is tested for proper operation. Since a functional unit may consist of a computer and its operating system, system test time in some cases includes the time for testing computer programs belonging to the operating system. 4.9 Hot Standby A configuration in which redundant equipment is kept in an operational mode so that it can be automatically brought into service should the primary equipment fail. 4.10 Reconfiguration The modification of a configuration of a functional unit in the event of a.failure or an error for the purpose of bringing that functional unit into a state in which it can perform its required function. 4.11 Cold Standby A configuration in which redundant equipment is kept idle or performing secondary functions and can be manually brought into service should the primary equipment fail. 4.12 Fail Safe A design property of a functional unit by which, in the event of a failure, it assumes a prescribed safe state. 4.13 Failsoft Pertaining to a computer system continuing function because of its fault tolerance. 4.14 Error Recovery 4.3 Operable Time The time during which a functional unit is capable of yielding correct results, if operated. 2 The process of correcting or bypassing. the effect of a fault to restore a computer system to a prescribed condition. to which a user's unit time during which a

~nintenar~e performed existing fhults. 3.6 Controlled

Maintenance

The use of techniques to sustain a desired quality of service in order to minimize preventive maintenance and reduce corrective maintenance. 3.7 Preventive Maintenance specifically to prevent

Maitztenance performed failures from occurring. 3.8 Scheduled Maintenance

Preventive maintenance carried out with an established time schedule. 3.9 Remote Maintenance

Maintenance performed over a communication link, with the assistance of, or under the control of, a maintenance facility in a separate location at which a higher level of knowledge and expertise is available. 3.10 Marginal Test/Marginal Check

A maintenance technique in which certain operating conditions are varied about their nominal values in order to detect or to locate potential faults. 3.11 Diagnostic Pertaining to the detection. analysis, tion of faults, failures, or mistakes. 3.12 Microdiagnostic A diagnostic technique by which a special purpose microprogram is incorporated in, or externally based as necessary, afunctional unit. 3.13 Test and Maintenance Program unit and or descrip-

A program designed to test a functional primarily for the purpose of maintenance verification operation. 4 AVAILABILITY 4.1 Availability

The ratio of the total operable time, excluding maintenance time, to the total time a functianal unit is required for use. 4.2 Serveability The ability of a service to be obtained at the request of the user, and to continue to be provided for a requested duration within specific tolerances and under given conditions.

A state in which a functional perform its required functioning. 4.20 Burn in

A circuit or program that ensured that a functional unit is operational by periodically generating a signal that, unless acknowledged by the unit within a prescribed period of time, activates an alarm or causes redundant equipment to take over. 4.17 <TO> Logout

A process of increasing the reliability of new or refurbished hardware by operating it in a prescribed environment and by performing corrective maintenance at every failure encountered, with a view to eliminate as many early faults as possible. 4.21 Rerun Time

To save into a storage the internal status of a functional unit in the event of afailure for the purpose of facilitating maintenance. 4.18 Logout Analysis

That part of operating time used for reruns to failures or mistakes in operating. 4.22 Redundancy
